claims.statement: The client-readable record is exactly start_fen, moves, plies, outcome, turns and error (RECORD_KEYS); these keys are annotated OmitFromInput, so they appear in output but are ignored if a caller sends them.

The turn working channels (allowed_moves, candidates, candidates_by, proposal, fallback_move, consumed_message_ids, terminal_intent, failed_call, invocation) are PrivateStateAttr and excluded from the input/output schemas, but the thread-state API still returns them, so clients must read only the record keys.
The agent input schema has exactly two properties, messages and position; position is OmitFromOutput and ChessCore clears it to None on every run.

messages are the model's working context rather than the game record: position commands are converted into synthesized delta HumanMessages, rejected chat messages are removed with RemoveMessage, illegal attempts add feedback messages, non-LLM moves get a synthesized 'MOVE: <san>' AIMessage, and summarization may remove the message a Ply.message_id references.
On the first run, even a rejected or no-op one, ChessCore writes an empty record (standard start_fen, empty moves/plies/turns, outcome and error None) because LangGraph omits never-written keys.

A Ply records ply index, side, uci, san, source ('external' for input moves, otherwise the proposal source), analysis, message_id, turn_id, model, latency_ms and meta keyed by middleware name; external plies have null message_id, turn_id and model and zero latency.

When a move commits, the ply's model is the last llm call's model for LLM proposals and proposal.meta['model'] otherwise, its latency_ms is the finalized turn's latency, its meta is gathered from each extension's ply_meta(), and the turn becomes committed with ply set to the new ply's index; if the move ends the game, the same update sets outcome and a result message.

A TurnRecord stores id, a request fingerprint (the chat message id or position:<sha256> of start FEN, moves and sorted restrict), initial_allowed, status (pending, committed, abandoned, terminal), ply, calls, rejected/feedback message ids, opened_message_id, illegal_attempts and latency_ms; turns records every turn, including those that produced no move.

Extension model calls reported through turn_calls() and time reported through turn_latency_ms() are folded into a turn's calls and latency_ms exactly once, when the turn commits, becomes terminal, or is abandoned.

A Call records kind (llm, systemone, summary), canonical provider:model, token counts that may be null when unreported, the 1-hour cache-write subset, called_at, cost_usd (null if unknown or unreported), cost_complete and the genai-prices version.

packages/chess-ui/src/types.ts is a hand-maintained mirror of the Python state types (Outcome, Call, TurnRecord, Ply, and ChessValues for readable keys) plus the server's ChessContext and setup, and must be kept in step manually.
The UI reads messages only to stream the live reply: liveAnalysis returns the latest AI text after the pending turn's opened_message_id, skipping replies already committed to a ply.

UI selectors depend on record links: turnOf finds a ply's turn via turn_id, lastPolicyPly returns the last non-external ply, isPending checks the last turn's status, and turnCost sums a turn's priced calls, marked incomplete if any call is unpriced or approximated.

A run carries one command: a chat message (the newest unconsumed HumanMessage, which must be 'go' or one legal SAN/UCI move, recorded as an external ply) or a position; sending both is rejected with 'send a position or a message, not both'.
position.restrict must be non-empty and contain only legal moves; the turn's allowed moves are the legal moves intersected with restrict, in legal-move order, stored as initial_allowed.

Resubmitting the same command (same message id or position fingerprint) is a no-op after its turn committed and a retry while it is pending; a run with no command likewise retries a pending turn or is a no-op.
A retry finalizes an already-validated proposal or resignation rather than calling the model again; otherwise it resets decision state and restores allowed_moves from the turn's initial_allowed.
While a turn is pending, a new chat message is rejected ('finish or retry the pending turn first') and removed, whereas a new position marks the pending turn abandoned and opens a new turn.

A thread is one game: a position command is rejected if its root differs from a thread with moves ('a different starting position; use a new thread') or if its moves do not start with the thread's moves ('the position does not extend this game; use a new thread'), including a new restrict on a shorter move list.

Position commands are replayed from the root with an ending check before each ply, so invalid FENs, illegal moves and moves after a game-ending position are rejected with CommandError messages that become the error field.

A rejection writes only error, invocation 'reject' and a cleared position (plus the first-run empty record) and ends the run, leaving moves, plies and turns unchanged; accepted commands, retries and no-ops reset error to None.
Once outcome is set, any command is rejected with 'the game is over' and empty runs are no-ops; this check precedes replay because a resignation cannot be rederived from the board.

If a command's resulting position is already over (checkmate, automatic draw, or with draw_claims='auto' an actual threefold or fifty-move draw), core records a terminal turn, the outcome and a result message without calling the model, and the run's invocation is noop with opened_turn set; draws merely claimable by the next move are not adjudicated.
Exhausting illegal-reply retries produces a resignation outcome and a terminal turn with ply None.

The UCI adapter replaces its thread (deleting the old one) when the GUI position does not extend the current thread's game (takeback or new game), and filters searchmoves to legal moves so it never widens the restriction; if all searchmoves are illegal it sends an empty restrict, which the agent rejects.
Without a checkpointer the agent is stateless and each run starts a new game from its own input.
The write guard rejects extension writes to core-owned ChessState keys; extensions may write only allowed_moves, proposal, fallback_move, candidates and their own declared keys.

The Agent Server adds a client-readable setup key (OmitFromInput, not private) via GameSetupMiddleware, holding asdict of the run's resolved ChessContext; it is written only by the run that opened the game's first turn (one turn whose id equals invocation.opened_turn) and never rewritten afterward.

GameSetupMiddleware checks in both before_agent and after_agent so a first turn whose model call fails still records setup and a first command that ends the game (which jumps past later before_agent hooks) records it too; a rejected first input or a thread created before setup existed never gains one.
The web UI continues a game from its thread's setup value and returns no game for a thread without a readable setup rather than guessing a context.
invocation.opened_turn names the turn the current run opened and is None for retries, rejections and plain no-ops.

When a model call fails after some provider calls completed, ChessCore keeps those calls and their time on the turn, sets the private failed_call marker, and after_model re-raises the original error in the same run.
illegal_attempts is counted on the durable TurnRecord, so a retry after a provider error keeps the remaining illegal-move budget rather than resetting it.
